lang_en:
The tandoors were still cold when my friend Tanvi and I reached the lane.
She was hungry, so she turned back toward Teen Darwaja to eat anywhere else.
Then I read the NakshIQ note I'd skipped: don't walk in before nine.
We waited on wet stones until the first tandoor caught with a low roar.
Over tava biryani and chicken angara, Tanvi, who had wanted to leave, asked for seconds.
Their families have cooked here since they fed the sultan who founded this city.
This is Bhatiyar Gali, and the city is Ahmedabad.
Travel intelligence is knowing when a place wakes up.
NakshIQ.
lang_hi:
जब मैं और मेरी दोस्त तन्वी उस गली में पहुँचे, तो तंदूर अभी ठंडे पड़े थे।
उसे भूख लगी थी, तो वो कहीं और खाने के लिए तीन दरवाज़ा की तरफ़ वापस मुड़ गई।
फिर मैंने NakshIQ का वो नोट पढ़ा जो छोड़ दिया था: नौ बजे से पहले मत आना।
हम गीले पत्थरों पर रुके रहे, जब तक पहला तंदूर भक से जल नहीं उठा।
तवा बिरयानी और चिकन अंगारा आया, और जो तन्वी वापस जाना चाहती थी, उसी ने दोबारा मँगाया।
इनके परिवार तब से यहाँ खाना बना रहे हैं, जब इन्होंने इस शहर को बसाने वाले सुल्तान को खिलाया था।
ये है भटियार गली, और शहर है अहमदाबाद।
ट्रैवल इंटेलिजेंस है ये जानना कि कोई जगह कब जागती है।
NakshIQ.

shots: Night, close on a row of cold clay tandoors along a narrow Old City lane, lids on, no flame, wet stones shining under a bare bulb, no people, no readable signage.
Wide shot from behind at night: two friends in their late 20s, a man and a woman, walk up the wet lane a clear step apart, each with hands in their own pockets, already in frame, no readable signage.
Medium shot from the side at night: the woman stands a little apart from the man with her phone in hand, half turned back the way they came, both faces turned from camera.
Close at night on one clay tandoor as the first flame catches inside it and sparks lift into the dark, no people in frame.
Over-the-shoulder at an open-air stall counter at night: steel plates of tava biryani and chicken angara, the woman's hand pulling a second plate toward her, her face out of frame.

Wide at night: the two friends sit a little apart at a lit open-air stall counter with steel plates in front of them, tandoor fire glowing and smoke drifting under bare bulbs behind them, several stalls lit down the lane, nobody else in frame.
